title: SN1987A in the Large Magellanic Cloud
caption: Supernova 1987A and the Tarantula Nebula in the Large Magellanic Cloud, imaged by the ESO Schmidt Telescope
celestial: Large Magellanic Cloud, LMC, SN 1987A · constellation Dorado · about 170000 light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: Official ESO press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: A very bright star stands out in the middle right of this view of the Tarantula Nebula, which lies in the Large Magellanic Cloud. That star is Supernova 1987A. When the image was taken, the supernova was bright enough to see with the unaided eye.

A supernova is the explosion of a star, and for a time it can outshine huge numbers of ordinary stars. The Large Magellanic Cloud is a small galaxy near our own, and the Tarantula Nebula is a large region of glowing gas within it. The scene lies about 170000 light-years away, in the constellation Dorado.

The photograph was taken with the ESO Schmidt Telescope, a type of telescope built to cover a wide area of sky in one shot. That wide view places the supernova within its surroundings in the Large Magellanic Cloud.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (49.61 x 67.84 arcminutes) and distance (170000 light years), the frame spans roughly 2,500 × 3,400 light-years. Its light set out about 170,000 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the ESO 1-meter Schmidt telescope. The color mapping isn't published.
understand.eye: At the time, the supernova itself could be seen without a telescope, while the photograph gathers far more light than the eye.
